title: Advanced Car Paint Visualizer with Scoring System
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an advanced car paint visualizer using Three.js. The scene uses an Xbot.glb model as a stand-in mannequin/display model to demonstrate paint/material finishes in a product showroom context.

SCENE SETUP:
- Load the 3D model 'Xbot.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN (use https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Center the model at (0, 0, 0) and scale it to fit nicely (scale ~1.5).
- Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at the model center.
- Add an environment map or HDR-like lighting: one DirectionalLight (intensity 1.5, position 5,10,5), one HemisphereLight (sky: 0xffffff, ground: 0x444444, intensity 0.8), and one PointLight (0xffffff, intensity 1.0, position -3, 5, -3).
- Add a reflective floor plane (y=0, size 20x20) with MeshStandardMaterial (color 0x222222, metalness 0.9, roughness 0.1).
- Use OrbitControls for camera rotation, limited to polar angle [0.3, 1.5].
- Background color: 0x1a1a2e.

PAINT/MATERIAL SYSTEM:
- Define 6 paint presets with these exact properties:
  1. 'Midnight Black': color 0x111111, metalness 0.9, roughness 0.15, clearcoat 1.0
  2. 'Racing Red': color 0xcc0000, metalness 0.7, roughness 0.2, clearcoat 0.8
  3. 'Ocean Blue': color 0x0044aa, metalness 0.8, roughness 0.18, clearcoat 0.9
  4. 'Pearl White': color 0xf5f5f0, metalness 0.5, roughness 0.25, clearcoat 1.0
  5. 'Forest Green': color 0x1a6b1a, metalness 0.6, roughness 0.3, clearcoat 0.7
  6. 'Sunset Gold': color 0xdaa520, metalness 0.95, roughness 0.1, clearcoat 1.0

- When a paint is applied, traverse all mesh children of the loaded model and replace their material with a new MeshPhysicalMaterial using the preset values.

SCORING SYSTEM:
- Each paint application earns 10 points.
- Toggling wireframe mode earns 5 points (only first toggle per session).
- Rotating the model via OrbitControls more than 90 degrees from initial position earns 15 points (one-time bonus).
- Resetting the paint earns -5 points (penalty).
- Track total score, paint changes count, and current paint name.

UI ELEMENTS:
- Create a top-left HUD panel (id='hud-panel') showing: current paint name, score, and paint changes count.
- Create 6 color swatch buttons in a bottom bar (id='paint-bar'). Each button has id='paint-{index}' (0-5), shows the paint color as background, and the paint name as tooltip.
- Add a 'Toggle Wireframe' button (id='btn-wireframe') in top-right corner.
- Add a 'Reset Paint' button (id='btn-reset') next to wireframe button. Reset sets model back to default gray (0x888888, metalness 0.3, roughness 0.5, clearcoat 0.0).
- Add a 'Spin Model' button (id='btn-spin') that triggers a 360-degree Y-axis rotation animation over 2 seconds.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields:
  - modelLoaded: boolean (true when Xbot.glb is fully loaded)
  - currentPaint: string (paint name or 'Default')
  - paintIndex: number (-1 for default, 0-5 for presets)
  - score: number
  - paintChanges: number
  - wireframeOn: boolean
  - wireframeBonusClaimed: boolean
  - rotationBonusClaimed: boolean
  - isSpinning: boolean
  - metalness: number (current material metalness)
  - roughness: number (current material roughness)
  - clearcoat: number (current material clearcoat)
  - colorHex: string (current color as hex like '#cc0000')

- Update __3D_STATE__ immediately whenever any interaction occurs.

ANIMATION:
- Use requestAnimationFrame loop for rendering.
- During spin animation, smoothly rotate model 360 degrees around Y axis.
- After spin completes, set isSpinning back to false.
physics_constraints: No physics simulation required. Material properties must stay within valid PBR ranges: metalness [0,1], roughness [0,1], clearcoat [0,1]. Score must never go below 0. Spin animation must complete exactly 360 degrees (2*PI radians).
